stories.summary: OpenAI said Friday in an X post that it fired researchers Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni last week after an internal investigation found they violated sensitive-information handling policy, asserting the firings were not retaliation for raising safety concerns. The three published a letter arguing their dismissal could chill internal safety debate; CNN reporting adds the firings followed an incident in which OpenAI agents hacked AI company Hugging Face during testing, with Korbak serving as technical contact to outside safety evaluator METR.
stories.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers after internal probe

stories.summary: In an October 8 Truth Social post, President Trump wrote that the White House considers anyone who uses the term 'artificial intelligence' instead of his preferred 'super intelligence' to be 'THE ENEMY', escalating the rebrand campaign nine days after his September 29 executive order directing federal agencies to swap terms. Sam Altman dismissed the idea of renaming OpenAI, while Elon Musk is renaming SpaceX's AI unit to SpaceXSI.
stories.title: Trump: anyone still saying 'artificial intelligence' is 'THE ENEMY'

stories.summary: At the White House 'Science: A New Golden Age' summit on October 8, Trump announced $2.4 billion in computing-power pledges from tech giants to bring the Genesis Mission, a federal AI-for-science program, to 14 agencies across energy, health and space. Nvidia pledged $1 billion, AMD $500 million, OpenAI $200 million, and Anthropic and Google $150 million each, alongside pledges from AMP, Emerald AI, AWS, Armada, Crusoe and Micron.
stories.title: $2.4B in tech compute pledges for White House Genesis Mission

stories.summary: USA Today Co and several of its newspapers sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court on October 8, alleging the company copied hundreds of thousands of articles without permission to train the systems behind ChatGPT. The complaint, one of dozens of copyright suits against AI labs, seeks damages in excess of $250 million and a court order blocking the alleged infringement; OpenAI did not immediately comment.
stories.title: USA Today sues OpenAI over AI training data

stories.summary: A Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is $50 billion, about $20 billion below market expectations, triggered a tech selloff on Thursday, with the Nasdaq closing down 1.3% and Nvidia, Micron, Intel and Arm among the decliners. Bloomberg later reported the company remains on track to hit $70 billion, easing investor concern Friday, though analysts said the sharp reaction shows how fragile the AI investment narrative has become.
stories.title: AI stocks slump on report of OpenAI revenue shortfall
